events.title: USD Falls Below G. 6,000 for First Time Since 2018 (2026-08-05)
events.summary: The US dollar fell below G. 6,000 for the first time since 2018, trading at G. 5,920 (buy) / G. 5,970 (sell) at exchange houses as of August 5. The BCP reference rate stood at G. 5,966.06. The guaraní has appreciated nearly 25% in ten months from almost G. 8,000/USD, driven by a record soybean harvest, global dollar weakness, and reduced demand for dollarization of guaraní-denominated income. The BCP maintains a neutral stance with no FX intervention.

events.title: Paraguay Records -0.1% Deflation in July as Food and Import Prices Fall (2026-08-04)
events.summary: Paraguay registered consumer price deflation of -0.1% in July 2026, driven by lower food prices and cheaper imported goods (vehicles, electronics) resulting from the strong guaraní. Annual inflation stands at approximately 2.1%, well below the BCP's 3.5% target. The BCP projects year-end inflation at 3.3%, revised downward from 3.5%.

events.title: Dollar-Denominated Lending Surges 67% as Borrowers Bet on Weak Dollar (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Foreign-currency credits surged 22.47% year-on-year to USD 13.7 billion, with the services sector alone expanding 67%. Businesses and individuals are increasingly borrowing in dollars to take advantage of the strong guaraní, though this exposes them to exchange rate risk if the dollar rebounds. The IMF has flagged rapid consumer credit growth as warranting close monitoring.

events.title: Agricultural Machinery Imports Jump 30% on Strong Guaraní and Agribusiness Boom (2026-08-05)
events.summary: Paraguay imported 1,893 units of agricultural machinery worth USD 177.4 million in the first half of 2026, a nearly 30% increase year-on-year. Tractor imports surged 44.5%, sprayers 66.7%, and seeders 1.6%. The boom reflects both the record soybean harvest and the favorable exchange rate making imported capital goods cheaper in guaraní terms.

events.title: President Peña Promises Zero Debt with State Suppliers by 2027 (2026-08-06)
events.summary: President Santiago Peña pledged to clear all outstanding government debts to suppliers by the 2027 fiscal year, with accumulated obligations exceeding USD 1.27 billion, of which approximately USD 1 billion is owed to the Ministry of Health for medicines, supplies, and services, and USD 220 million to the MOPC for construction companies. A USD 2 billion 30-year bond issuance has been proposed as a financing mechanism.

events.title: New Fiscal Convergence Plan Sets Deficit Path: 3.2% in 2026, 1.5% by 2028 (2026-08-07)
events.summary: The government presented a new Fiscal Convergence Plan setting deficit targets of 3.2% of GDP for 2026, 3.9% for 2027, and a return to the Fiscal Responsibility Law limit of 1.5% by 2028. Business groups (ADEC) endorsed the plan but called for improved quality of public spending. Economist Sergio Sapena warned that the real fiscal deficit may be closer to 4% of GDP with USD 2 billion in accumulated hidden debts, potentially threatening the investment-grade rating.

events.title: Paraguay Signs '123 Agreement' on Civil Nuclear Cooperation with the US (2026-08-05)
events.summary: Paraguay signed the '123 Agreement' with the United States for civil nuclear cooperation, joining over 25 nations with similar agreements. The MoU enables transfer of civilian nuclear technology for energy and scientific purposes under IAEA oversight, following the discovery of uranium deposits in Paraguay with US investment in exploration.

events.title: Government Advances New Mining Code to Unlock USD 2 Billion in Investments (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Following discussions with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the Peña administration is advancing a new Mining Code to unlock an estimated USD 2 billion in mining investments, according to the Paraguayan Mining Chamber (Capami). The code may also open possibilities for hydrocarbon and mineral exploration in protected areas such as Médanos del Chaco National Park.

events.title: National Doctors' Strike Called for August 24–28 Amid Healthcare Crisis (2026-08-07)
events.summary: The National Doctors' Union (Sinamed) called a nationwide strike for August 24–28, demanding salary adjustments to recover 2012 purchasing power levels, double pay for holiday shifts, permanent appointments for approximately 9,000 doctors on precarious contracts (many with over 10 years of service), and provision of basic medical supplies. Union president Rosanna González described the situation as one of the worst crises in Paraguay's public health system.

events.title: Police Leadership Replaced in Alto Paraná as Security Crisis Deepens (2026-08-05)
events.summary: The Police Directorate of Alto Paraná department replaced its commander (Crio. José Félix Vega replaced by Crio. Jorge Ramón Aquino Aguayo), a move interpreted as recognition of the failure to contain escalating organized crime. The most dramatic incident occurred on June 16 in Santa Rita, where over 20 armed criminals simultaneously attacked three banks and an exchange house using explosives and rifles. The government launched Operation 'Responsum', deploying combined police and military forces.

events.title: Police Brutality and 'Gatillo Fácil' Cases Draw National Outcry (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Última Hora documented multiple cases of police brutality, including a journalist (Lorenzo Villalba) beaten and tortured while filming police operations, two brothers receiving a 30-minute beating and chemical assault in a police cell, and a 22-year-old man killed by 37 bullet wounds (one to the head) at a police checkpoint in Alberdi, Ñeembucú. The report characterized these actions as reminiscent of dictatorship-era practices.

events.title: Double Homicide in Encarnación Linked to Gold Transaction; Five Foreign Nationals Arrested (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Two Paraguayans were murdered during an alleged gold transaction in Encarnación. Five foreign nationals were arrested: three Bolivians and two Spaniards (father and son). The victims were restrained, bound, and shot; the robbery involved approximately G. 370 million. The case highlights growing organized crime activity linked to gold smuggling in border regions.

events.title: VP Alliana: Paraguay-US Relations at 'Best Moment in History' as Bilateral Agenda Expands (2026-08-04)
events.summary: Vice President Pedro Alliana and Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez visited Washington D.C., meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Deputy Secretary Chris Landau. Key outcomes included the signing of a nuclear cooperation MoU (123 Agreement), discussions on the 'Shield of the Americas' security initiative, and collaboration on critical minerals under the Pax Silica framework. President Peña also held a phone call with Rubio on August 3, characterizing the bilateral agenda as 'spectacular.'

events.title: Paraguay Co-Sponsors OAS Foreign Ministers' Meeting on Nicaragua Crisis (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Paraguay co-sponsored a US-led initiative at the OAS to convene an extraordinary meeting of foreign ministers on Nicaragua, with Ambassador Raúl Florentín declaring that Ortega's plans to eliminate free elections 'compromise hemispheric security.' The meeting was proposed to occur before September 2026, when constitutional reforms are planned. Paraguay joined Argentina, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Uruguay, and the US in the initiative.

events.title: Taiwan Grants 76 Scholarships to Paraguayan Students as 70th Anniversary of Diplomatic Ties Approaches (2026-08-07)
events.summary: Taiwan's embassy in Paraguay awarded 76 scholarships across various disciplines, bringing the total to 894 scholarships granted since 1991. The two countries are preparing to mark the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027. Paraguay remains Taiwan's sole diplomatic ally in South America and the only Mercosur member without ties to China. President Peña visited Taiwan in May 2026; China strongly condemned the visit.

events.title: Mercosur-EU Trade Deal Enters Provisional Application; Paraguay Demands Equitable Export Quotas (2026-06-29)
events.summary: The Mercosur-EU free trade agreement entered provisional application from May 1, 2026, eliminating tariffs on over 90% of traded goods across a 700-million-person market. At the June 29 CMC meeting, Foreign Minister Ramírez demanded 'equity, not privileges' in EU export quota allocation, rejecting distribution based solely on historical trade volumes as 'unreasonable' for Paraguay and warning it undermines real market access.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: Second 5G Auction Concludes: Tigo Wins 2.3 GHz, Personal Wins 3.7 GHz (2026-08-06)
events.summary: CONATEL concluded its second 5G spectrum auction, awarding Tigo the 2.3-2.4 GHz band (100 MHz) and Personal the 3.7-3.8 GHz band (100 MHz). Both operators have 180 days to launch commercial services (deadline February 2027). Each committed to invest at least USD 40 million in secure network infrastructure with trusted-vendor equipment. License duration is only 5 years — the shortest in Latin America, raising concerns about return on investment.
events.client_tag: Tigo, Personal — 5G spectrum acquisition, USD 40M+ investment each

events.title: Bloomberg Highlights Paraguay as Regional Leader in Clean Energy and AI Destination (2026-08-07)
events.summary: Bloomberg featured Paraguay as the Latin American country with the greatest potential to attract technology infrastructure investments, noting it is the only country in the region with 100% renewable electricity generation. The report highlighted that every 100 MW of energy can attract approximately USD 4 billion in data center investment. Electricity rates are among the world's most competitive: ~USD 0.046/kWh commercial vs. global average of USD 0.164/kWh.
events.client_tag: Data center and AI operators — Paraguay positioning as regional clean energy hub for AI infrastructure

events.title: Paraguay-Taiwan AI Hub Megaproject Announced: Three-Phase Plan to 1 Gigabit Capacity (2026-05-11)
events.summary: President Peña announced a 50/50 joint venture with Taiwan to build one of the world's largest AI centers in Paraguay, combining Taiwanese semiconductor technology (90% global share) with Paraguayan hydropower. The three-phase plan targets: Phase 1 — 10 MW data center, Phase 2 — 100 MW, Phase 3 — 1 GW. Peña compared the ambition to the construction of Itaipú. Location and construction timeline are yet to be disclosed.
events.client_tag: Huawei, ZTE, data center equipment suppliers — large-scale infrastructure opportunity

events.title: HIVE Digital Launches First AI GPU Cluster in Paraguay, Plans 100 MW Expansion (2026-08-08)
events.summary: HIVE Digital Technologies launched Paraguay's first AI GPU cluster at a Tier III data center in Asunción, running production workloads with Columbia University researchers for LLM training. HIVE operates approximately 300 MW of hydroelectric infrastructure in Paraguay with another 100 MW in development. A large-scale HPC expansion is planned for 2027, with additional Tier III data center capacity in Yguazú, positioning Paraguay as a bridge for AI computing between New York and Asunción.
events.client_tag: NVIDIA, GPU suppliers, data center infrastructure vendors — compute infrastructure opportunity

events.title: Tigo (Millicom): Wins 2.3 GHz 5G Spectrum; IDB Invest + Proparco Inject USD 100M; Local Bond Raises USD 77M (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Tigo secured the 2.3-2.4 GHz band in Paraguay's second 5G auction with 180 days to launch commercial service. In March 2026, IDB Invest and Proparco committed USD 100 million via a private bond to Millicom for 4G/4.5G/5G network modernization and fiber expansion across Latin America, including Paraguay. Tigo Paraguay also raised approximately USD 77 million in a landmark local-currency bond issue in January 2026. Tigo is the market leader with 3.16 million mobile internet users and posted a 56.3% adjusted EBITDA margin in Q1 2026. Paraguay represents approximately 11% of Millicom's group revenue.
events.client_tag: Millicom/Tigo — 5G rollout, network modernization, fiber expansion; network equipment, infrastructure

events.title: Personal (Telecom Argentina): Wins 3.7 GHz 5G Spectrum, Leads FTTH Market (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Personal won the prime 3.7-3.8 GHz band in the second 5G auction (same band used by parent Telecom Argentina). The company was recognized by Ookla at MWC Barcelona 2026 as having the fastest fixed network in Paraguay. Personal (operated by Núcleo S.A.) leads the FTTH market with aggressive urban fiber deployment and is the second-largest mobile operator with 1.66 million users. The 180-day deployment deadline for 5G commercial launch places the target in February 2027.
events.client_tag: Telecom Argentina/Personal — 5G deployment, FTTH expansion; network equipment, fiber infrastructure

events.title: Claro (América Móvil): First 5G Network Operational Since Dec 2025, Plans Nationwide Expansion (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Claro Paraguay activated the country's first 5G network in December 2025 with an initial USD 35 million investment and Nokia infrastructure, covering Greater Asunción, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación, Coronel Oviedo, and Pedro Juan Caballero. Claro acquired 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band (USD 2.02 million) in the 2025 auction. General Manager Alfredo Alcaraz confirmed continued expansion throughout 2026. Claro is the third-largest operator with 947,000 mobile users.
events.client_tag: América Móvil/Claro — 5G network expansion, nationwide coverage; Nokia infrastructure, network equipment

events.title: Nubicom Under Investigation for 5G Non-Compliance; USD 200M Pledge Unfulfilled (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Argentine ISP Nubicom, which won 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band in the 2025 auction with a pledged USD 200 million investment, is under investigation by the Comptroller General for failure to comply with spectrum deployment obligations. No 5G network deployment has been reported nearly one year after the license award. The case raises concerns about the viability of new entrants in Paraguay's 5G market and may lead to spectrum reclamation.
events.client_tag: Nubicom — non-performing 5G license; potential spectrum reallocation opportunity for existing operators

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business Operations
sections.impact_analysis: 🟡 Exchange Rate & Competitiveness: The guaraní's sustained appreciation (G. 5,952/USD, down ~25% from G. 8,000 ten months ago) creates a dual-edged business environment. Importers of capital goods (machinery, telecom equipment) benefit from cheaper dollar-denominated purchases, as evidenced by the 30% surge in agricultural machinery imports and 67% jump in dollar loans. However, exporters and companies with USD-denominated revenue face margin compression. The BCP's neutral intervention stance suggests the strong guaraní will persist, requiring businesses to hedge FX exposure more actively. 🔴 Fiscal Risk: While Paraguay's investment-grade ratings (Moody's Baa3, S&P BBB-) remain intact, the real fiscal deficit may be closer to 4% of GDP with approximately USD 2 billion in hidden supplier debts. The government's Fiscal Convergence Plan targets a return to the 1.5% legal limit by 2028, but execution risk is significant. Any downgrade would raise sovereign borrowing costs and could trigger capital outflows. The proposed USD 2 billion 30-year bond issue would add to the public debt burden (currently 38.1% of GDP). 🟢 Opportunity — Digital Infrastructure: The convergence of 5G auctions (all three major operators now hold spectrum), Bloomberg's recognition of Paraguay as a clean-energy AI destination, the Taiwan AI hub megaproject, and HIVE's first GPU cluster deployment signal a structural shift toward Paraguay as a regional digital infrastructure hub. Companies supplying telecom equipment (massive MIMO, fiber, data center infrastructure), cloud services, and AI compute should position now. The 100% renewable grid and USD 0.046/kWh commercial electricity rates are globally competitive advantages that are unlikely to erode. 🟡 Security & Operational Risk: The deterioration of security in Alto Paraná (bank heists by armed commandos, police leadership changes) and growing organized crime linked to gold smuggling (Encarnación double homicide) raise operational risk for businesses with logistics, branch networks, or personnel in border departments. The national doctors' strike (August 24-28) will disrupt public healthcare access, potentially affecting workforce availability and productivity. 🔴 Regulatory Uncertainty — Telecom: CONATEL's decision to grant 5G licenses for only 5 years (versus the 15-20 year international standard) creates significant regulatory risk for telecom operators' return on investment. The exclusion of Chinese equipment vendors (Huawei, ZTE) from 5G deployments, while politically aligned with US interests, limits technology options and may increase deployment costs. Nubicom's non-compliance investigation further clouds the regulatory landscape.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis: 🔴 High Risk — Diplomatic Constraints: Paraguay remains Taiwan's sole diplomatic ally in South America. President Peña's May 2026 visit to Taiwan and the approaching 70th anniversary of bilateral ties (2027) reinforce the status quo. China has repeatedly condemned these moves and stated there will be no trade benefits without recognition of the One-China Principle. Chinese enterprises face potential reputational risks and should conduct thorough compliance reviews before entering Paraguay-linked projects. The 5G equipment exclusion (Huawei, ZTE) is a direct manifestation of this diplomatic alignment and is likely to persist under current policy. 🟡 Medium Risk — Indirect Market Access: Despite diplomatic barriers, Chinese goods dominate Paraguay's import basket (mobile phones, computer equipment, tires). Chinese enterprises can continue serving the Paraguayan market indirectly through regional subsidiaries in Brazil, Argentina, or Chile, or via trading intermediaries. The Mercosur-EU trade deal's provisional application opens additional indirect trade channels. Chinese telecom equipment vendors should explore partnership models with non-Chinese integrators or focus on enterprise/private network segments not covered by the public 5G auction restrictions. 🟢 Opportunity — Infrastructure & Energy: Paraguay's USD 480 million railway project (Asunción-Luque corridor, led by UAE's Etihad Rail under G2G agreement) and the proposed USD 2 billion mining code investments represent large-scale infrastructure opportunities where Chinese contractors and equipment suppliers could participate through consortium arrangements with non-Chinese partners. The three-phase Taiwan AI hub project (up to 1 GW) will require massive power infrastructure upgrades — Chinese electrical equipment and transmission technology could be sourced indirectly. 🟢 Opportunity — Agribusiness & Machinery: The 30% surge in agricultural machinery imports demonstrates strong demand for capital goods. Chinese manufacturers of tractors, harvesters, irrigation systems, and agro-processing equipment, while facing brand perception challenges, can compete on price-performance in a market where the strong guaraní makes imported equipment more affordable. Joint ventures with Brazilian or Argentine distributors already operating in Paraguay offer a viable entry strategy. 🟡 Caution — Security & Labor: The healthcare strike and security deterioration in border departments (Alto Paraná) are localized but can disrupt operations. Chinese enterprises with expatriate staff or field operations in these areas should review security protocols. The minimum wage increase to PYG 3,044,000 (+5% from July 2026) and the statutory 16.5% IPS employer contribution mean that labor costs, while still among the lowest in Latin America, are rising. Proper workforce planning should account for the aguinaldo (13th month) and mandatory benefits.
